featured_reviews.name: Rajat Bajaj
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Vig Restaurant for an authentic Sindhi breakfast experience, and it turned out to be a delightful culinary morning. Located in the heart of Chembur Camp, this well-known Sindhi eatery truly lives up to its reputation for serving traditional flavours at very reasonable prices.

I ordered the classic Dal Pakwaan, and it was everything one expects from a proper Sindhi breakfast. The pakwaan was beautifully crisp, light yet crunchy, and perfectly fried without being greasy. It paired wonderfully with the flavourful dal, which was well-seasoned and comforting. The serving came with aloo subzi, chutney, pyaaz, and pickle, creating a complete and satisfying platter. Every bite had the right balance of spice, tanginess, and texture.

One of the highlights of the visit was their heart-shaped tikki (pattice). Not only was it visually appealing, but it was also deliciously crisp on the outside and soft inside, packed with flavour. It added a special charm to the breakfast spread.

To complete the meal, I enjoyed a chilled mithi lassi — thick, refreshing, and perfectly sweet. As a Punjabi, I always appreciate a good glass of lassi, and this one truly hit the spot. It complemented the spicy breakfast beautifully and made the experience even more enjoyable.

The service was prompt and courteous, adding warmth to the overall visit. The restaurant maintains a simple, authentic vibe that reflects Sindhi culture and hospitality. It felt homely, welcoming, and genuine.

Overall, Vig Restaurant offers a wonderful taste of traditional Sindhi cuisine in Mumbai. Delicious food, generous portions, reasonable pricing, and pleasant service make it a place worth revisiting for a hearty and satisfying breakfast.

featured_reviews.name: swayambharat
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sweet Blind Spot!
While there are enough places serving the usual popular fare- Punjabi, South Indian and Chinese, its kind of difficult to find good Sindhi food baring a few like Nanumal Bhojraj (OG-masjid bunder), Gurukrupa (sion) and Bhagat Tarachand (OG- Kalbadevi) but thats it!
Vig happily fills that void and how!
Just go there on a Sunday morning and one can see a crowd just for takeaways, as the kitchen churns out piles of puris, parathas, kulchas deftly being packed along with Chole, Dal, Chutney and handed over to this never ending stream of customers.
Been yearning to visit Vig in Chembur for ages, and when we landed there, took parcel of an assortment of Aloo Tikkis, Dal Pakwan and Chole Bhature.
More than me, our friends instantly fell in love and planned a visit soon for a repeat!

featured_reviews.name: Ayyub Kolsawala
featured_reviews.review_text:
My favorite thing to do on a Saturday morning is breakfast. So, we drove off to Chembur for the famous Sainath Kulchas. While they serve a variety of Kulchas, through trial and error I have figured out my favorite one.

Firstly, There are a few things that Sainath does that make their Kulchas perfect, the "barrel shaped" tandoor & the quality of the ingredients.

The Aalu Cheese Kulcha 🔥: Delicious Aalu filling with lots of cheese. Baked until crispy in the tandoor. They finish the kulcha with a dollop of butter & sprinkle some Jeera powder to add more flavour. The melted cheese & aalu filling goes great with the crispy kulcha making it the best one in the house! Try the Paneer Kulcha too.

Chola 👎: All the kulchas are served with Chola & some onion salad. However, the chola is never tasty.

Recently they have also introduced a place where you can sit and enjoy the Kulchas. I prefer the comfort of my car though 😇 (if you can find a spot to park).

Bonus:

After the Kulchas, you should try the sugarcane juice right next to it. You could also try the Lassi at Vig. Oh this place takes cash only, the UPI Scanner doesn't work.

featured_reviews.name: Krishnam Mimani
featured_reviews.review_text: This place is at the entrance of a lane right opposite to Ganesh mandir in chembur camp. Consider this place as street food because there's no seating as such. It can only accommodate 4(sitting) persons at a time in the shop. If you go during the afternoon then prepare to be roasted in the sun while eating. The food is average, nothing too great. This place is specifically for kulcha and the chola is like a side dish. I travelled all the way from kalbadevi after watching a reel by some food blogger and I am disappointed. It's not worth the travel. If you live close by and take the food parcel then it might make sense cause this place is affordable. I ordered a alu pyaaz and paneer cheese kulcha and both tasted pretty regular, nothing that would set these apart from any other restaurant. Kulchas are made in a proper tandoor that's all. The total was 180rs which is reasonable. The chole lacks flavours and it's better to have the kulcha without the chole. I honestly don't understand the hype about this place. Only visit this place if you live in the area, otherwise it's not worth the travel.

featured_reviews.name: Divyesh Bora
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sindh Pani Puri Centre in Chembur is a well-loved destination for street food enthusiasts, particularly for those craving a delightful pani puri experience. Known for its consistent quality and authentic flavors, this spot stands out for its exceptional Dahi Pani Puri, a popular variation of the traditional snack.

The Dahi Pani Puri at Sindh Pani Puri Centre is a refreshing take on the classic dish. Each puri is perfectly crisp and golden, providing the ideal vessel for the delicious fillings. The stuffing is a flavorful blend of mashed potatoes and chickpeas, spiced just right to offer a savory contrast to the sweet and tangy toppings. The puris are generously topped with chilled, creamy yogurt, which is smooth and rich, balancing the flavors beautifully.

The addition of tamarind chutney and a sprinkle of chaat masala elevates the dish, adding a burst of sweet and tangy notes that dance on your taste buds. The freshness of the ingredients is evident, making each bite a delightful experience.

The bustling atmosphere at Sindh Pani Puri Centre adds to its charm, with friendly vendors serving up these delightful treats with speed and a smile. Whether you're a seasoned street food aficionado or trying Dahi Pani Puri for the first time, Sindh Pani Puri Centre offers an authentic taste of Mumbai's vibrant street food culture that is not to be missed.

featured_reviews.name: All IN ONE
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Flavorful Experience at Vadapav Café – A True Street Food Gem

If you’re someone who loves authentic Indian street food served fresh, with a touch of care and quality, Vadapav Café is a place that should be on your must-visit list. Located in a modest yet inviting stall-style setup, this café manages to capture the essence of Mumbai street flavors while also ensuring that the food is made with 100% groundnut oil — a detail that might seem small but makes a world of difference in taste and health.

From the moment you walk up to the counter, the aroma of freshly fried batata vadas and sizzling bread pakodas hits you. The place is run by people who clearly know and love what they are doing. The staff work quickly but with precision, making sure that every vadapav is perfectly assembled — crisp from the outside, soft and fluffy inside, with chutneys spread just right.

---

Vadapav – The Star of the Show

Let’s start with the classic: the regular Vadapav. At just ₹25, it’s the perfect definition of “value for money.” The pav is lightly toasted, the vada is golden brown and perfectly spiced, and the chutneys (a mix of spicy red chili, tangy tamarind, and fresh green coriander) complement each other beautifully. The first bite is a delightful balance of textures — crunchy, soft, and smooth — and flavors ranging from mildly spicy to tangy and savory.

The Butter Vadapav takes things up a notch. The pav is toasted generously with butter, giving it a richer taste and an indulgent aroma. It’s one of those small upgrades that turns an everyday snack into something you want to savor slowly.

Then comes the Cheese Vadapav. If you’re a cheese lover, this one is pure joy. The molten cheese oozes into every bite, mellowing out the spice while adding creamy depth. And if you’re feeling extra indulgent, the Double Cheese Vadapav is an absolute treat — gooey, rich, and unforgettable.

---

Bread Pakoda – Crispy Comfort Food

If vadapav is the king, the Bread Pakoda is the loyal queen of Indian street snacks. Priced at ₹25 for the regular and ₹40 for the butter version, these are crispy on the outside, soft and flavorful inside, and fried to perfection in groundnut oil, which gives them a clean, non-greasy finish.

For those who can’t resist cheese, the Cheese Bread Pakoda (₹90 for 2 pieces) is heavenly. The melted cheese inside the batter-coated bread, paired with the crunchy crust, is the kind of snack that makes you forget all about counting calories.

featured_reviews.name: Kartikeya Pathak
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Flavorful Delight: Spicopedia Restaurant Review, Jio World Drive Food Court

I recently visited Spicopedia restaurant in the Jio World Drive food court, and I was blown away by the flavors and authenticity of their dishes. We tried a variety of options, and each one was a winner.

Vada Pav
The Vada Pav was an absolute showstopper - it reminded me of the iconic Ashok Vada Pav from Dadar, and it was absolutely lip-smacking in taste. The vada was crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside, and the pav was soft and lightly toasted. The combination was pure magic.

Bhel Puri
The Bhel Puri was another delicious option - it was a perfect balance of sweet, spicy, and tangy flavors, with a delightful crunch from the sev and onions.

Paneer Makhni and Dal Makhni with Tandoori Roti
We also tried the Paneer Makhni and Dal Makhni with Tandoori Roti, which were both good options. The paneer was creamy and rich, and the dal was flavorful and comforting. The tandoori roti was soft and lightly charred, perfect for sopping up the sauces.

Service
The service at Spicopedia was friendly and efficient, with our food arriving promptly at our table.

Ambiance
As a food court stall, Spicopedia doesn't have a traditional dining ambiance. However, the stall itself is well-designed and inviting, with a cozy atmosphere that makes you feel like you're in for a treat.

Verdict
Spicopedia restaurant in Jio World Drive's food court is a must-visit for anyone craving authentic and delicious Indian street food. With its lip-smacking Vada Pav, delicious Bhel Puri, and satisfying Paneer Makhni and Dal Makhni, it's a spot that will leave you feeling satisfied and eager to return.

Price: Moderate (around ₹600-₹800 per person)

Recommended for: Foodies, street food lovers, and anyone seeking a delicious and authentic Indian meal.

Will I return?
Absolutely, to try more of Spicopedia's delicious dishes!

Cos of the veg array

I keep coming back to this vegetarian restaurant, and if I’m being honest, geography is doing a lot of the heavy lifting here. It’s conveniently close enough that my laziness can overpower my cravings for a while.

The food is fresh, well-made, and clearly prepared with care. The menu does a commendable job of convincing vegetables to impersonate things they were never meant to be. Some dishes even come dangerously close to making me forget about real food- meat.

Unfortunately, I was raised on a steady diet of creatures that once had opinions, so my deeply ingrained bias toward real food remains the ultimate buzzkill. Every bite is accompanied by a tiny voice in my head asking, “This is nice, but we paying
Fr veggie food bro?”

That said, if you’re vegetarian, you’ll probably love it. If you’re a carnivore like me, you’ll still enjoy it—especially if it’s close enough that convenience can temporarily defeat instinct.

Would return. Mostly because it’s nearby. Partly. Thats it

A little disappointing to not be able to try a best seller item because they didn’t have it. We tried the Babyback ribs, Mushroom pasta and tenderloin burger. The babyback ribs were good but served with a side of French beans coated in a milky sauce. The mushroom pasta was very good. The burger was nice but served with what tasted like stale Mota chips. Overall the food was nice but strictly average considering the price. There are plenty of other restaurants that have food that tastes exactly the same, so nothing that would call me back.

featured_reviews.name: khanapina. in
featured_reviews.review_text:
SAZ in BKC is one of those places that instantly wraps you in its warm, modern brasserie vibe the moment you walk in. With its chic interiors, dim-gold lighting and a playlist that feels curated for good moods, it’s the perfect blend of classy and comfortable — the kind of place you can go for a cosy brunch, a fun dinner date, or post-work cocktails that turn into long conversations.

The menu leans into American comfort with a gourmet twist, and almost everything that lands on the table has the “I want to take a picture first” aesthetic. Think bold flavours, generous portions, and dishes that balance indulgence with finesse.

From small plates to mains, every dish has its own personality — nothing bland, nothing boring. Their ingredients taste fresh, execution is neat, and the flavours hit that satisfying spot without being overly heavy.

The cocktails deserve their own chapter. SAZ is known for its bar game, and it shows — well-balanced drinks, interesting mixes, and something for every palate. Whether you like punchy, fruity, smoky or spirit-forward, you won’t feel short of options.

Service is smooth, attentive and friendly without being in-your-face. The staff actually knows the menu and recommends things based on what you like, not just what’s trending.

Overall, SAZ BKC is the perfect spot when you want a guaranteed good time — amazing food, great drinks, a stylish ambience and a vibe that feels both lively and relaxed. It’s the kind of place you walk out of thinking, “Yep, we’re coming back.”

featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a lovely experience at Saz. The food, ambience, and service — everything was really good, and the place has a great vibe for a relaxed meal.

We tried the prawn tostadas, which were nice but slightly too sour for our taste. We also had the black garlic bread, pizza, and ravioli. The pizza and garlic bread were absolutely delicious and definitely the highlights of the meal. The ravioli was good, though a bit on the sweeter side than expected.

For dessert, we had the salted caramel ice cream, which tasted nice but was slightly melted when served, which was a small letdown.

Overall, it was a very pleasant experience, and I would definitely visit again to try more dishes from their menu.

​A few tips for your visit:
​Skip the Mutton Vajidi fry: It was just okay. If you really want Vajidi, head to Theresa Hotel nearby instead. 🚩
​Logistics: The place is very small and gets incredibly congested. 👥 On weekends, expect to wait 30+ mins for a table and another 15 mins just for service. They also charge a ₹5 dine-in fee. 💸
​Best Strategy: Visit on weekdays before 3 PM for the Biryani. 🕒
​Parking: Car parking is a nightmare due to the narrow street; bikes are much easier. 🛵
​Pro Tip: Unless you are a very patient group, I highly recommend taking a parcel 🥡 and enjoying it at home! 🏠

featured_reviews.review_text:
Hitchki s one of the most popular restaurants in Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC), known for its Bollywood-inspired interiors and innovative Indian menu. The moment you walk in, the lively ambience, desi décor, and upbeat music set the tone for a great dining experience. It’s a perfect spot for casual dinners, celebrations, and influencer-friendly content.

We tried a mix of starters, mains, and desserts, and every dish delivered on flavour. The Nacho Nacho Regular was crunchy and addictive, while the Mangalorean Roast Chicken brought authentic coastal flavours to the table. The Godfather Chicken was rich and indulgent, and the Malvani Kolambi Masala stood out with its bold spices and perfectly cooked prawns—easily one of the best seafood dishes in BKC.

Dessert lovers should not miss the Lotus Biscoff Tiramisu, which was smooth, creamy, and beautifully balanced. Paired with their signature drinks like BBC, Hitchki (BKC) proves why it’s among the best restaurants and bars in BKC. Highly recommended for great food, lively vibes, and a memorable dining experience.

They have great menu with innovative names for all their dishes making it even more exciting to order. The service is very fast and good. The drinks are worth trying and of great innovation. 1) BIHARI KEBAB: It had Specialty Of Chef Dipesh + Age Old Recipe + Dry Masala Rub +
Tandoori Chicken + Tamatar Chutney. Must try.

2) CAESAR CHICKEN TIKKA: It had Parmesan Malai Marinade + Tandoor Cooked Chicken +
Garlic Parmesan Aioli.

3) ASIAN KITCHEN (CHICKEN): We customised it with Hakka Noodles + Manchurian Garvy + Chicken added. Really tasty and amazing.

4) DESI GIRL COCKTAIL: It has Tequila, Orange Marmalade, Desi Magoi Masala Punch, Red Wine Float + Chakna on top, perfect for a drink.

5) DEEWAR COCKTAIL: It has Whisky + Spiced Jaggery + Bitters + Apple Wood Smoke, amazing presentation and worth trying.

White Chocolate Ganache + Cherry Gel + Milk Chocolate Shavings.

featured_reviews.name: Rimita D
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Hitchki at BKC, around 7-10 minutes from Kurla station by auto/4 wheeler. It's a vibrant Bollywood themed restaurant and a perfect evening party spot. The presentation of every dish was top-notch.
We tried Masala Soda, Main Toh Superman, Tiger Jhinga Hai, Prawns Jaaye Par, Pressure Cooker Chicken Tikka Biryani, Godfather Chicken, and Lotus Biscoff Tiramisu all impressive, especially the above appetizers which are highly recommended. Chicken lovers must try the Godfather Chicken for its great portion size and taste.
Lotus Biscoff Tiramisu wasn’t overly sweet and made a perfect ending. Loved the playlist too, you will surely vibe on it. Special thanks to Salman and the entire team for the excellent service.

featured_reviews.name: Prakash Dhalwani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Hitchki BKC is a great spot for a fun lunch or evening out! The vibe is absolutely lovely — beautiful interiors with a cool bar-like feel that makes the whole experience enjoyable.

We tried quite a spread — nachos with cheese, garlic cheese bread, truffle fries, butter chicken seekh kebab, and paneer chilly, and everything was delicious! The truffle fries and seekh kebab were personal favourites. The only miss for us were the butter garlic prawns, which didn't quite live up to the rest of the menu.

Service was prompt and attentive, and we didn't have to wait long for a table at lunch — always a bonus! Valet parking is available which is super convenient for BKC.

Overall a solid dining experience and would definitely recommend it for the vibe and food. Will be back to explore more of the menu! 🙌

featured_reviews.name: Jinal Tank
featured_reviews.review_text: We tried a variety of dishes at Hitchki and had a great experience. The spring rolls and fried dumplings were crispy and tasty. Paneer makhani was rich and creamy with soft naan, while the noodles with Manchurian gravy were flavorful and filling. The dessert with ice cream was a perfect sweet ending, and the mocktails were refreshing. Overall, good food, nice presentation, and worth a visit.

featured_reviews.name: Raunak Bhutani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Have been visiting hitchki bkc for over 6 years but the recent visit left no desire for us to be back again.
Ordered their new Dhurandar chicken which was quite average, the rotis served with it were a disaster, they felt raw hardly even roasted in the tandoor. When we conveyed the same to the person who served us (who also turns out to be the manager) was straight up arrogant and replied that he could only microwave it. Yes sure only forgetting that this isn't some random canteen where he is doing us a favour of serving food.
The basics of service is to first listen here it's the opposite when he gives us such great suggestions.
Such arrogance when the restaurant was almost empty on a weekend lunch would leave the restaurant much emptier in the future as it should be.
Having recommended hitchki to so many would have to do the opposite this time.
The second order Nasi goreng was extremely stale, the satay alongside was not hot, the preparation extremely salty.
Nothing worked apart from the parle G dessert which at least provided some sweetness to our rather sour experience.
